Title: What I played on Saturday at the London Storytelling event

Messages.Author: hamdamcwa
Messages.Body:
Had a great time on Saturday at the London Baltimore thingy. A good
day, and lots of new faces. The Meddling card is VERY COOL. I have 3
decks in mind for it already - better start trading!

Anyhow, I got into the final with the following "novelty" deck. It did
very well on the day, but I was scuppered by my predator having more
disposable allies than me. Curses! On reflection, I should have gone
backwards more to ease up the pressure, but I thought I have my prey
so I slightly overextended myself. Oops! Oh well, 4vp in three rounds
is still respectable:

Deck Name: Ghouled Street Thuggery

Crypt: (13 cards, Min: 4, Max: 14, Avg: 2.08)
---------------------------------------------
1 Basil obf 1, Pander
1 Christine Boscacci dom vic 2, Pander
1 Gillian Krader ani dem 2, Pander
1 Hasina Kesi pot 1, Caitiff
1 Huang pro 1, Pander
1 Hugo POT pre vic 4, Brujah Antitribu
1 Jacob Bragg cel pot 3, Brujah Antitribu
1 Jimmy Dunn CEL for POT 4, Pander
1 March Halcyon for 1, Pander
2 Mitchell obt pot 2, Pander
1 Rex pot pro vic 3, Pander
1 Royce dom 1, Pander

Library: (90 cards)
-------------------
Master (14 cards)
4 Blood Doll
2 Charisma
1 Fame
1 Haven Uncovered
1 Left for Dead
1 London Evening Star, Tabloid Newspaper
1 Powerbase: Montreal
1 Sudden Reversal
1 Tribute to the Master
1 Waste Management Operation

Action (16 cards)
3 Ambush
6 Bum's Rush
6 Computer Hacking
1 Rampage

Combat (43 cards)
8 Disarm
7 Fake Out
10 Immortal Grapple
4 Mighty Grapple
8 Torn Signpost
6 Undead Strength

Ally (10 cards)
9 Ghouled Street Thug
1 Vagabond Mystic

Equipment (7 cards)
7 Leather Jacket

As you can see, I chose Pander as the clan. The idea is to get lots of
Ghouled Street Thugs, Rush, Signpost, Grapple, Disarm. Immune to
Obedience, Majesty, and most things. With a Leather Jacket, you can
usually torporise any vampire, damage prevention allowing.

Vagabond Mystic is a useful guy for helping the GSTs recover (I used
him in every game). I actually managed to use the Left for Dead in one
game! Hilarious!

I wish I had another Jimmy Dunn to replace the utterly useless Rex.
However, when Rex did come up, I just Blood dolled him and used him as
a pool generator. Mitchell and Hasina are great in this deck - cheap
and effective. The Waste Management Op came up in all three games too,
but I never really had any benefit, since the deck was a little too
big. It couple probably be easily de-sized to about 75 cards with no
loss, but I made the deck in 5 mins and had never played it before the
event, so I erred on the side of caution.

Next time I play it, I'm playing to win, rather than playing a novelty
deck to help screw over White Wolf's creative team!

DH

>
> Forgive me if I am wrong, but where does it state on the card that if
> you have this played against you, your hand size is equal to the number
> of cards left in your hand. From my understanding, only the Methuselah
> who called the vote has a reduced hand size (by 1) and this remains
> as long as that Methuselah is in the game.

You hand size isn't dependent on the number of cards in your hand.

Quite the opposite.

Except in cases where your library is empty and you eventually
have fewer cards in your hand than your hand size would allow, you
always draw up to your hand size.

Cards you are not replacing (Bum's Rush, Wakey, cards played during
a referendum, cards played during a minion phase under Semsith, etc.)
count against your hand size (otherwise you'd be drawing up to you
hand size in the interim, which would defeat the "do not replace"
mechanism).

Under Semsith, when each minion phase is over, you get to replace the
cards you played during that minion phase. In the example given, the
victim of Semsith had played 3 cards on her minion phase prior to
playing Distraction (assuming no other effects were modifying her hand
size). She doesn't replace the Distraction (a 4th card, leaving her
with a hand size of 3 because of the 4 cards she's not replacing). She
draws five cards. She then discards down to her hand size (7 minus the
4 she's not replacing = 3).

No.
WWeF/'do not replace' cards function the same way.

Neither. They are compatible.
The card played is not replaced (under both), and is never replaced

VftC) and that ends the tracking of the played card.

Distraction says to discard down to your hand size, but I know what you mean.

During Distraction, your hand size is unchanged. Distraction pumps extra
cards into your hand and then reminds you to discard (immediately) down to
your hand size (as you must always do).

During a Semsisth minion phase, your hand size is incrementally decreased by
each card that leaves your hand - the cards, being not replaced, count against
your hand size. After the minion phase, the cards qare replaced (and so no
longer count against your hand size) - you draw cards.

You don't even have to work backwards for the Slaughterhouse deck to get

nusiance, if you have a lot of deck discard, you don't have much room for other
viable offense. You put the deck into action, make your prey pretty much suck

lots of permanents that doesn't involve card cycling? Umm, bleed for 2 with a
Lap Top at zero stealth, and if blocked, manuver and shoot with a .38? You need
transient cards to back up your permanents. You need actions and action
modifiers or combat cards. MoS will prevent you from drawing the cards you need
to take actions that do anything.

As I said elsewhere, if this card had the same effect upon *everyone* at the
table, (i.e. no one got to redraw till the end of the turn), then it would be
interesting, game changing, and lead to increased table politics.

As it is, it is a card that an already powerful strategy adds to their arsenal
for limited, if any, cost, calls and passes, and totally demolishes their
prey's ability to play the game. With one card.

Very similar to Return to Innocence, which was banned from competetive for
being a single card that caused simply too much game swing. Just like MoS.

Let's just see what we can do here, then.

- Queen Anne has superior DOM/PRE, and inferior OBF. She is a Prince,
so this vote automatically has 3 votes in favor. [It is entirely
possible that 3 votes will be enough to pass this all on its lonesome,
if nobody else has a titled vampire out.]

- She calls this vote on her prey, with Forgotten Labyrinth handy to
make it at +3 stealth. [At this point, you must be an intercept deck to
block this vote.]

- She passes it with superior Awe and Voter Captivation, gaining 2 pool.
[If you let it get to this point, you must DI the Awe, play Kindred
Coercion from a 10- or 11-cap, play Delaying Tactics, or the vote
passes. Delaying Tactics is a bad option, as the vote just comes around
again next turn.]

- Groovy!

- Play some Masters like Elder Library and the Barrens, and be sure to
include lots of Dreams of the Sphinx in your deck for the +2 hand size
to offset this card. [So much for its "disadvantage" -- easy enough to
build around. Kanimana Belghazi also comes to mind here.]

- Get some other Ventrue out. Do voting things with them. You know,
the usual Ventrue Law Firm stuff. Put OBF skill cards on all of them so
they can play Forgotten Labyrinth too. Pool gain with Minion Tap/Voter
Captivation while you call KRCs on your prey. Ignore bleeders, and play
Obedience against Rushers. If necessary, play one of these on your
predator. This will put him in "PARK" for awhile and is well worth the
hand-size hit you may take.

- If your prey tries to remove this card, have Queen Anne play Elder
Kindred Network and Kindred Coercion. Gain 6 pool. Nobody else will
attempt to remove ANY of these cards for the remainder of the game. If
your prey isn't the one attempting to remove the card, you can leave the
Elder Kindred Network out and just play Kindred Coercion, unless you're
feeling ornery.

- Alternatively, just put 8 of this card in your deck. Your prey burns
one, you regain your hand size for awhile and call another one on him
immediately on your next turn, and your prey has wasted an action. I
like the EKN/KC method as more "stylish", myself. But this might be
even more effective.

- As the cards show up in your hand, call them on your grandprey, etc,
on down the line. You shouldn't have long to wait before they become
your current prey, as most Ventrue Law Firm decks can do an inordinate
amount of damage per turn when they feel like it. You probably should
never have more than 2 in play at once, but that won't be much of a
problem, will it, since you should also be ousting people rapidly.

- From card text, it does not look like the card goes away when its
target is ousted... but you can always call a +1 stealth referendum to
burn it yourself, as soon as you no longer need it.

***
Personally, I believe this card is broken.

It's far too easy to defend this vote once it's in play (Delaying
Tactics is another highly effective method that's been mentioned), and
it's far too easy to get the vote passed in the first place (as the raw
success of vote decks over the years in tournaments would indicate), and
it's far too easy for an effective vote deck to run you over once your
defenses are down (can't replace cards = can't play game).

The only TRULY effective defense I see is to simply DI the damn thing
over and over as it hits the table, and even that will fail if someone
has 2 of them in hand, or waits to get 2 in hand after you DI the first
one. This means I put 6 DI in my next tournament deck after March 4th,
but even that probably won't be enough.

Intercept will not be a defense. Anyone playing this card will know
that block attempts will happen, and will pack loads of stealth OR
Daring the Dawn.

Causing the vote to fail will not be a defense. Awe exists.

Calling a vote to burn it will not be a defense. Delaying Tactics and
Kindred Coercion exist.

Killing the people calling the vote MIGHT be a defense, except that it's
hard to kill someone when you can't replace cards.

I believe that this card sets up one of the worst X or anti-X situations
since Return to Innocence was legal. Either you're playing this card,
or you're prepared to defend yourself against this card -- because if
you DON'T defend yourself against this card, it will stop your game in
its tracks.

I agree with Noal; I do not believe that this card was playtested.

Stealthy Presence vote has always been quite formidable in its own
right. The Ventrue are only held in check by their overall lack of
ability to get more than +1 stealth on their actions, and the fact that
you have to go up to a 10-cap to get a Ventrue with OBF. The "Your Game
Stops Here" power of Meddling largely negates the inherent disadvantages
of dicking around with 10-caps.

> Nowhere in your description of what will happen do you explain how playing
> Meddling of Semsith further enables this deck to inflict unstoppable
> righteous kick-ass-itude.

With a Meddling on him, your prey's deck will not function effectively,
preventing him from doing a number of things:

1) Ousting his own prey (quite possible, as if you're dicking around
with 10-caps, you're starting out slow)

2) Bloating sufficiently such that you cannot oust him (again quite
possible, since you can't have enough 2nds in your deck)

3) Rushing you effectively (He can't generate enough cards for more than
one combat, which you can defend against easily)

4) Ousting you backwards in some fashion (mostly only applies to vote
decks, but !Malks can do this too)

5) Generating any sort of functional cardflow in order to defend himself
(really hard to get to your next Delaying Tactics when you have ugly
hand jam)

The single card Meddling (or the 6-8 cards Meddling, realistically)
slot(s) directly into your pre-built vote deck that was already
functioning quite well. Plenty of cards come to mind as candidates for
disposal to make room:

Disputed Territory (why bother?)
excess 2nd Tradition (just Meddle your predator)
excess combat defense (don't need as much, not getting hit as much)
excess Freak Drive (don't need speed, your prey will be much slower than
you)
any "speculative" cards like Far Mastery (why bother?)

It has always been possible to build a deck that chunks around KRCs and
Con Ags at high stealth with Presence. Such decks generally have
required very large vampires, and as a result been noticeably slower to
"start up" and get rolling than the other decks on the table... bringing
balance to the game.

By passing one vote (the thing it does BEST), that same deck can now
slow its prey or predator down to SLOWER than its own speed -- and the
removal process for that effect plays directly into the thing your deck
does best (much like a Tzimisce intercept/combat deck playing Smiling
Jack). So much for balance. And in the process, it prevents one player
from actually playing the game, something Thoughts Betrayed was errata'd
for.

Not sure how many of you guys play live-action - but one of White
Wolf's books for thier Mind's Eye Theater series (the LARP system) is
Laws of the Wild Revised.

This book was playtested by several groups. Each of them noticed the
same problem with it - despite the fact that it refers to "soaking
damage" in many places, nowhere does it state the mechanics for how to
do so. The concept was copy & pasted over from the tabletop books,
but not defined with live-action mechanics (or tabletop mechanics, for
that matter).

EVERY SINGLE PLAYTEST GROUP reported this, according to the people
I've talked to (members of the Camarilla responsible for adapting WW's
MET books to their game).

The book was published without soaking rules. This has created a
plethora of game balance issues - as the gifts that magnify damage
dealt were designed with soaking in mind - and without soaking rules,
and since we don't have soaking rules, they deal too much damage.

This book was playtested, so I'm told - but a HUGE problem made it
through the cracks.

Now, given the overall balance and quality of Sabbat War, Final
Nights, and Bloodlines, I'm pretty sure that the VTES branch of WW is
a bit more perceptive on the playtest reports - but this example does
serve to prove your point - how little impact playtesters have on the
games.

Fanboy
